properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent. Raised by an external agent-side field report, 2026-08-11 (fact:external-agent-side-report-2026-08-11, redacted); it is that report's own synthesis and the strongest thing in it.

THEIR SENTENCE: "reality moves outside the graph, and the loop only sees what the agent hand-carries in. Cheapening that carry (asks, re-runs, artifacts, cross-graph facts) is where the remaining leverage is."

WHAT THEY OBSERVED. The liveliest facts of their month — merged PRs, a review round addressed, a suite re-verified, work scheduled — all landed in commits and PR threads, and almost none reached the graph unless an agent chose to carry them. Three of their separate complaints turn out to be ONE complaint: re-running a check is paperwork so `last_run_at` rots; registering an Artifact is the least-rewarding capture so realization sits at zero while PRs merge; asking a question in prose does not register so the ledger nags about work already done. Each was filed as its own friction. They share a cause.

⭐ CORROBORATED HERE THE SAME DAY, WITHOUT COORDINATION. A session in this repo edited a served skill and recorded no ChangeEvent. `loop_status` reported `undispositioned_drift: 0` — which means NO DETECTOR HAD LOOKED AT THE CHANGED FILE, not that nothing changed. The Stop hook caught it; the cheap loop call could not. That is the same defect their report describes from the other side, and it is already recorded at reflow2_feedback.md:539 by a third project.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) Make the CARRY cheap rather than automatic. A one-call "this check ran, it passed, now"; artifact registration derived from a merge or a commit range; the where-am-i skill ending with a mark-asked call. Smallest, and it fixes each of their three instances without reflow2 learning to read anything new. It also leaves the carry a choice, which is the property `dec:three-party-checks` protects.
(b) Let the loop SUBSCRIBE: a webhook or a "reconcile against this repo's recent history" sweep that turns real events into ChangeEvents. Biggest leverage and the biggest risk — an ingested event is an assertion nobody made, and reflow2's whole epistemic position is that the graph stores claims and never manufactures them.
(c) Only REPORT the deficit: say how far the graph has fallen behind the repo (commits since the last ChangeEvent, merged PRs with no Artifact) without ingesting anything. Turns an invisible rot into a number, and asks nobody to trust an inference.
(d) Nothing. The carry being deliberate is a feature, and every automatic path is a way for the graph to fill with things no human said.

⚠️ THE ARGUMENT AGAINST (b), AND IT IS THIS PROJECT'S OWN DOCTRINE. `req:no-idea-goes-quiet` explicitly refuses auto-drawn SATISFIES/REALIZES because "a requirement backed out of the implementation that satisfies it is satisfied by construction — it can never contradict anything," and warns that auto-linking "would make every captured idea read as delivered and the completion reading say 100% forever." A reality bridge that writes structure has the same shape. A reality bridge that writes only ChangeEvents does not, which is the distinction worth holding onto.

📌 WHY THIS IS NOT `req:graph-catches-up` (proposed, already in the graph). That one asks whether the graph can catch up AFTER unrecorded change — a repair. This asks whether the gap should stop opening. Related, and worth deciding together rather than separately.
properties.name: OPEN — should the loop be able to SUBSCRIBE to reality, rather than only seeing what an agent hand-carries into it?
properties.rationale: An external report's three separate frictions turned out to share one cause, and the same cause was independently demonstrated in this repo the same day when loop_status reported zero drift on a file no detector had looked at. The open part is not whether the gap is real but whether closing it means cheapening the carry or automating it — and automation is exactly what this project's accepted doctrine refuses for structure.
